subject: Transition: Acme implementation plan + SDK/endpoint checklist
messages:

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Transition: Acme implementation plan + SDK/endpoint checklist

Hi Sam —

Congrats again on the contract. I wanted to kick off the formal CSM -> Implementation handoff so we have a single plan for SDK setup, endpoint migration, and retry/rate-limit expectations. Attached is a one-page checklist that covers the engineering milestones; please have your engineering lead confirm the timeline.

High-level asks for this sprint:
- Confirm target environment (prod vs. staging) and which Redwood deployment (hosted vs. dedicated) you want pinned by EOD Friday
- Share the IP allowlist and preferred KMS key name for private traffic
- Confirm max qps and average request size (tokens) so we can size batching and recommend quantization settings

I'll loop in Diego (implementation lead) and Marissa (solutions eng) who will take the technical onboarding. Diego: next steps are the SDK bootstrap, endpoint migration plan, and recommended retry/backoff settings.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-integration-checklist.xlsx

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <storres@acme-payments.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-18T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Transition: Acme implementation plan + SDK/endpoint checklist

Thanks Monica — looping up technical details. Sam, quick intro: I'm Diego, I'll be your implementation lead. Below is a concise SDK onboarding checklist and a minimal Node + Python snippet you can try in staging immediately. If you share a staging API key I can validate the handshake.

Minimal Node example (fetch-based):
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
async function generate(prompt) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <STAGING_KEY>', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small-1', input: prompt, max_tokens: 256 })
  });
  return res.json();
}

Python requests example:
import requests
def generate(prompt):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate', json={"model":"redwood-small-1","input":prompt}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer <STAGING_KEY>"})
    return r.json()

Endpoint migration notes:
- Use /v1/generate for now; we'll hand you a migration plan if you switch to a dedicated endpoint (dedicated endpoints keep the same surface area but a different host and API key).
- For bulk migration, send a representative workload for us to run in our optimizer; we'll return batching and quantization suggestions.

Retries & timeouts:
- Recommended client timeout = 30s (per call).
- Idempotency: generation calls are not idempotent; avoid retries without exponential backoff and jitter.
- Retry policy: 500, 502, 503, 504 -> retry up to 3 times with full-jitter exponential backoff starting at 200ms.
- Rate limit handling: when 429 observed, pause + exponential backoff and surface to metrics; for sustained 429s we recommend a token-bucket throttle on the client side.

I'll attach a small archive with code snippets and a JSON template for retry/backoff settings.

—Diego
Implementation Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sdk-snippets-v1.2.zip

Subject: Re: Transition: Acme implementation plan + SDK/endpoint checklist

Thanks Monica & Diego — forwarding to our eng lead. A few quick answers:
- We'll run initial testing in our staging cluster (staging.acme-payments.internal)
- Staging API key: will share via secure vault by EOD 11/19
- Expected steady-state qps: 8–12 requests/s; peak bursts up to ~45 req/s for checkout flows
- Typical request size: ~350 tokens average, peaks ~1200 tokens for batch jobs

Question on retries: if we hit consistent 429s during peak, would you recommend we migrate to Dedicated now or try aggressive client throttling first?

—Sam
Senior Engineer, Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <storres@acme-payments.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T10:13:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Transition: Acme implementation plan + SDK/endpoint checklist

Hi Sam — good context. Short answer: try client-side throttling + burst capacity first. Practical plan:
1) Implement token-bucket client with max burst = 3x steady-state (so burst ~36 req/s)
2) Add 429 circuit (if >5% calls 429 over a minute, degrade non-critical paths or route to a lower-cost model variant)
3) If after two weeks 429s persist at peak, we escalate to Dedicated evaluation (we'll provide a cost/latency delta).

Also: to preserve latency under batching, set a batch max latency of 50ms and max batch size tuned to your payload histogram (we can profile once you send sample traces).

I'll open IMPL-782 to track the work items and add a small runbook for the token-bucket config.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the update Sam — a couple of operational reminders before you flip the switch to prod:
- Log token-level cost and latency (we recommend emitting per-request metadata: model, tokens_in, tokens_out, region_hint); we'll ingest to the Redwood Console for cost projections.
- If you use our SDK, enable automatic retries flag with the policy Diego suggested — SDK v1.2 defaults to exponential jitter but you must opt in for generation path retries.
- For migration: we can create a dedicated endpoint preview for you for 48 hours to simulate peak traffic and validate tail latency. Let us know preferred window and we'll schedule.

I'll add the preview request to IMPL-782 and ping you once it's booked.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
